newsitem.title: USA: Unicom nuclear plant overhauling staff.
newsitem.headline: Unicom nuclear plant overhauling staff.

text.p: Unicom Corp.'s ComEd utility said Wednesday it had launched a reassessment of the operations staff at its troubled Zion, Ill., nuclear plant.

By April 2, about 180 operators and managers at the plant will be notified whether they will be rehired, transferred, or fired, according to a spokeswoman for the electrical utility that serves northern Illinois customers.

The move was prompted by a recent highly critical assessment of the plant by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), particularly after an incident last month in which one of Zion's twin reactors was mistakenly shut down by an employee and then restarted without permission.

In another case, workers repeatedly used a broom handle to flick a switch in a chamber that was slightly contaminated with radioactivity instead of donning protective garb and doing the job by hand. The handle was not decontaminated.

"We need to change our culture rapidly -- and to do that we need to quickly make sure our operators are leaders, people who can lead this plant to where we want it to be," John Mueller, vice president of the Zion plant, said in a statement.
The entire operations staff, which includes licensed engineers, will be evaluated. The plant employs a total of 900 workers.

The Zion plant, which is one of the nation's oldest, was among three of ComEd's six nuclear plants currently on the NRC's watch list. The utility also was fined $100,000 earlier this month for engineering violations at Zion.
